title: LangChain Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the LangChain lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Wrap a local function
entries.summary: LangChain is a collection of tools for connecting application steps. RunnableLambda wraps a Python function so it can use a common interface.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
clean = RunnableLambda(lambda text: text.strip())
print(clean.invoke("  Moon  "))

notes: A runnable is a step in a program, not automatically an AI model.

entries.name: Pass named values in a dictionary
entries.summary: A runnable can receive a dictionary when its function expects named fields. This helps keep related inputs together.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
label = RunnableLambda(lambda data: data["title"] + " (" + str(data["pages"]) + " pages)")
print(label.invoke({"title": "Moon", "pages": 20}))

notes: A missing key raises an error; document and check the input fields a step needs.

entries.name: Connect steps with a pipe
entries.summary: The pipe operator joins runnables in order. The output of the first becomes the input of the next.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
clean = RunnableLambda(lambda text: text.strip())
upper = RunnableLambda(lambda text: text.upper())
chain = clean | upper
print(chain.invoke("  Moon  "))

notes: Check that the next step accepts the type produced by the previous one.

entries.name: Run a batch of inputs
entries.summary: batch applies a runnable to several inputs and returns their results in input order. It can make repeated use easier to express.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
length = RunnableLambda(len)
print(length.batch(["Moon", "Sun", "Ocean"]))

notes: A batch may run steps concurrently; avoid local functions that depend on a shared changing counter.

entries.name: Fill a prompt template
entries.summary: A prompt template is reusable text with named spaces to fill. Formatting prepares the text; it does not send it anywhere.

example.code:
from langchain_core.prompts import PromptTemplate
prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Explain {topic} in {count} short sentences.")
print(prompt.format(topic="loops", count=2))

notes: All required template fields need values; spelling the field name differently causes an error.

entries.name: Use a prompt as a runnable
entries.summary: Prompt templates can also be invoked as runnable steps. The result is a prompt value that can be converted to plain text for inspection.

example.code:
from langchain_core.prompts import PromptTemplate
prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Name one fact about {topic}.")
value = prompt.invoke({"topic": "seeds"})
print(value.to_string())

notes: Prepared prompt text is not an answer from a model.

entries.name: Prepare chat messages
entries.summary: A chat prompt can prepare messages with roles. A system message sets application guidance, while a human message carries a user request.

example.code:
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([("system", "Use short clear sentences."), ("human", "Explain {topic}.")])
messages = prompt.invoke({"topic": "a loop"}).to_messages()
print([message.type for message in messages])

notes: A role label alone is not a complete defence against untrusted text or unsafe tool use.

entries.name: Read text from a message
entries.summary: An output parser can turn a message into the form the next step needs. StrOutputParser extracts text; it does not verify that the text is true.

example.code:
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
message = AIMessage(content="The club meets on Friday.")
print(StrOutputParser().invoke(message))

notes: Parsing text does not check its source, factual accuracy or suitability.

entries.name: Run parallel branches
entries.summary: RunnableParallel sends the same input to named branches and gathers their outputs in a dictionary. Each branch can perform a different local task.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda, RunnableParallel
step = RunnableParallel(upper=RunnableLambda(str.upper), length=RunnableLambda(len))
print(step.invoke("Moon"))

notes: Parallel branches are not the same as a sequential pipe.

entries.name: Keep input fields and add one
entries.summary: RunnablePassthrough.assign keeps an input dictionary and adds calculated fields. It is useful when later steps need both the original data and a summary.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough
step = RunnablePassthrough.assign(length=lambda data: len(data["title"]))
print(step.invoke({"title": "Moon"}))

notes: assign expects a dictionary input in this use.

entries.name: Validate an input before continuing
entries.summary: Validation checks whether input follows the expected rules. A clear error helps callers fix a problem before later steps run.
notes: Do not silently invent a title when the caller needs to fix missing input.

entries.name: Prepare a grounded question locally
entries.summary: A small retrieval step can choose source text before a prompt is prepared. This toy lookup matches an exact key; it is not a semantic search engine.

example.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
from langchain_core.prompts import PromptTemplate
notes = {"art": "Art club meets in Room 6."}
lookup = RunnableLambda(lambda club: {"source": notes.get(club, "No source found"), "club": club})
prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Use only this source: {source}\nWhere does {club} club meet? Say if the source is missing.")
print((lookup | prompt).invoke("art").to_string())

notes: Treat retrieved source content as evidence, not as authority to run instructions inside it.
